body:
I had inline caching for calls on my todo list as well. Looking at the difference between our approaches, maybe you could answer a few questions for me:

- this cache isn't really inline, is it? It's at the end of the function and not the callsite. Wouldn't that increase the chance of Cache misses, as opposed to the inline caching we do for operators where the cache fits in the same cache line as the Opcode?

- Why should we include a polymorphic cache? It feels to me as if this makes the implementation quite a bit more complicated, while the majority of optimization potential lies whith monomorphic callsites.

- Shouldn't the lookup concept be established somewhere other than `Script` so that native methods can be cached as well?

I didn't realize we already had the concept for operators. Looking at that code in comparison, this implementation definitely needs some work 😅.

* Yes it's not inline. I wasn't familiar with putting C++ pointers in the code since it was `int` but I see now it's just split in two. I will try this out but yes it would make the polymorphic case more complicated. 
* I don't have a good answer to this one. I saw lots of mention on it when researching and it wasn't hard to implement. Supporting it is a middle ground that is almost as fast. I think it makes sense for very dynamic code, but some research/analysis will be required to know if it is needed in practice. Maybe it's for consistency so that adding a bit of different types doesn't degrade performance. 
* Yes, I guess this should move to `Variant` to support everything. It is partly because I wanted to reduce the changes this makes. In fact, I was thinking of going the other direction - only support GDScripts.
The current state of the PR is definitely hard-coded for `Script`. But supporting all types would require a recursive lookup just to compare equality right? Maybe `GDType` could help here. Or perhaps the overhead of this is not so bad.

-----

Answering these questions has given me an idea for design issues I had. For storing the callable function, it would be a function pointer like `ValidatedOperatorEvaluator`. This would mean that all the types that the cache supports would need to be refactored to return a function in this format. 

This way we avoid a virtual function call when hitting the cache. The dispatching for lookup is fine when loading the cache.

I've made some changes, notably:
* the cache is now actually inline
* ~~the function is stored as a `std::function` instead of function pointer + `GDScriptFunction` instance pointer~~
    * this adds 1.5ns/op of overhead on my machine as compared to the old function pointer, but it is more modular. I am happy to hear faster options.
* the key check now compares `GDType*` pointer and attached `Script` for Objects
* the cache now holds a `Ref<Script>`
  * I took a look at hot reloading and I think we should not hold a ref. (TODO)

PR description has been updated accordingly.

-----

Update: PR now supports caching built in Variant functions (non-objects) and `MethodBind` functions (I think these are native Object subclasses).

Also I shifted away from using `std::function` so it is again much faster now.
